principles: Host-neutral workflow: commands and artifacts describe research lifecycle state, not a Codex-specific namespace.
Only fix real correctness and lifecycle-boundary issues; do not optimize or broaden the experiment arbitrarily.
Fail closed on spend approval, provider fallback, host-label snapshots, outcome rows, and premature Cell 06 execution.
Keep launch readiness separate from result evidence and paper/product claims.
Make status machine-checkable and readable for later hosts.
drivers: Product-reviewer INIT finding requires exact human-approved amount/currency/source for any nonzero budget cap.
The protocol requires Cell 03 before budget-lock generation and Cell 06 A2prime.
The user wants a DONE story without fake activation, fake provider execution, or stale/ambiguous state.

options.name: guardrail-only-cell03-launch
pros: Clears the real metadata discipline gap without spending budget or inventing approval.
Keeps Cell 06 and paper claims locked until real Cell 03 evidence exists.
Can be fully validated locally with negative controls.
cons: Does not produce provider outcome rows or H-M1/H-M3 evidence.
A later story is still needed for actual provider execution after explicit budget approval.

options.name: run-cell03-now
pros: Would produce real calibration records sooner.
Could start budget-lock derivation immediately after success.
cons: No exact nonzero budget approval, model snapshot IDs, or provider execution runner has been supplied in this thread.
Would risk provider spend and false readiness claims inside a story scoped for launch guardrails.

options.name: leave-current-disabled-state
pros: No risk of accidental provider spend.
cons: Does not solve the repeated ambiguity around what is missing before Cell 03 can launch.
Future agents may continue to confuse metadata readiness, execution approval, and result evidence.

rationale: Choose a Cell 03 guardrail-only launch package because it fixes the actual lifecycle correctness issue while refusing to invent budget approval or provider results.

preMortem.scenario: An agent interprets launch authorization as provider result evidence.
preMortem.trigger: Docs or checker say ready without restating no provider calls/outcome rows.
preMortem.consequence: Paper/product claims could be unlocked from metadata only.
preMortem.mitigation: Checker and status docs must assert no outcome rows, no H-M1/H-M3 proof, and no product gate impact.

preMortem.scenario: An implementer invents a nonzero budget cap.
preMortem.trigger: Artifact accepts amount without exact human-approved amount/currency/source.
preMortem.consequence: Provider execution could appear authorized without user spend approval.
preMortem.mitigation: Budget approval schema requires amount, currency, approvalSource, approvedBy, approvalDate, and providerSpendAllowed=false when absent.

preMortem.scenario: Cell 06 becomes unblocked before a real Cell 03-derived budget lock.
preMortem.trigger: Launch artifact uses Cell 03 readiness as a budget lock substitute.
preMortem.consequence: A2prime sequencing would violate the pre-registered protocol.
preMortem.mitigation: Checker negative controls reject Cell 06 unblocking and require realCell03DerivedBudgetLock.present=false in this story.

preMortem.scenario: Host labels are accepted as dated snapshots.
preMortem.trigger: Codex CLI or Claude Code CLI is written into executorSnapshot/reviewerSnapshot.
preMortem.consequence: Multi-model evidence becomes invalid because host and provider are conflated.
preMortem.mitigation: Snapshot validation rejects host labels and requires provider snapshot fields to remain non-host labels or absent.
